Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Redwood readiness: we can support the scope you described (LLM inference for customer support workflows) with options across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Key compliance items we discussed: SOC 2 status, GDPR data processing, HIPAA posture for PHI workloads, and your vendor questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ/custom).

Next steps I propose:
1) Can you share the formal questionnaire you want us to complete?
2) We'll draft initial responses and send back a completed spreadsheet + SOC 2 summary by EOD 3/5.
3) If there are technical clarifications, our SE (Dylan) can join a 30-min follow-up.

Attachments/notes: none on this email — please send the questionnaire when convenient.

Also answering two quick items from the call: we run encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and encryption at rest (AES-256) by default; we use AWS/GCP as subprocessors for Hosted. More details in the SOC 2 summary.

Thanks — looking forward to the questionnaire.

Best,

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmebank.com>

Subject: Re: Security questionnaire & SOC 2 follow-up — next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and for the details. Attaching our vendor security questionnaire (SIG-style Excel) and a data-flow template so you can map where customer data flows. Please complete the SIG/CAIQ where possible.

High-level clarifications we need up front:
- SOC 2: Do you have a Type II report? If so, we require delivery under NDA — is that possible?
- GDPR/HIPAA: Is Redwood capable of supporting HIPAA workloads (BAA)? Which deployment modes are supported (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)?
- Data residency: Can you confirm region controls for hosted deployments (US/EU)?
- Subprocessors: Can you provide a current list of subprocessors and what they process?
- Encryption: Confirm keys management (KMS/HSM) for customer-owned keys — available on Private or Dedicated?

Attachments: Acme_SIG_Questionnaire_2026.xlsx; Acme_DataFlow_Template.docx

Requested timeline: initial completed questionnaire by 2026-03-09. If you need more time, let us know. Our security team (cc) may follow up with technical evidence requests.

Thanks,
Sam Patel
InfoSec Lead, Third-Party Risk | Acme Bank
sam.patel@acmebank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmebank.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire & SOC 2 follow-up — next steps

Sam —

Thanks for sending the questionnaire and the data-flow template (received). We started an internal pass and attached our draft responses and a short SOC 2 summary for your review. See attachments: Redwood_SIG_answers_2026.xlsx; Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf.

Quick answers to the items you called out:
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering our hosted control plane and platform services. We can share the full report under NDA — happy to initiate an NDA if needed. The SOC 2 covers control categories relevant to your assessment (security, availability, confidentiality).
- GDPR: We process data in accordance with GDPR; we offer EU-region hosting for customers who require EU residency. We have a DPA available.
- HIPAA: We support HIPAA workloads on Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted customers, we offer contractual BAA options for certain enterprise customers; we should discuss scope (PHI vs outputs). Please confirm whether the data you plan to send contains PHI (PHI fields vs derived outputs).
- Subprocessors: Primary subprocessors include AWS (us-east-1/us-west-2), GCP (europe-west), and a managed logging provider. I included a short subprocessors list in the SOC 2 summary; we can provide a complete register.
- Customer keys: Customer-managed KMS is available on Dedicated and Private (we integrate with KMS/HSM). For Hosted, we offer managed encryption and can discuss Bring Your Own Key patterns for enterprise accounts.

Open clarifying questions for you (so we can answer the SIG fully):
1) Can you confirm the categories of data you consider PHI for this engagement? (e.g., full transcripts, PII fields, health codes)
2) Do you need pen-test reports or network diagrams as part of the initial deliverables, or will those come later?
3) Are there any additional supply-chain controls (e.g., specific vendor attestations) that your procurement team requires?

Proposed timeline from our side:
- 3/05: internal SE pass complete; send first-cut of completed SIG answers back to you.
- 3/09: target final delivery (assuming one round of clarifying Qs).

If that works, Dylan (cc) will take point on the technical evidence pack and I'll coordinate the contractual/NDAs. We can also schedule a 30-min follow-up with your security team mid-week — let me know availability.

Thanks — attaching the two files now.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: Redwood_SIG_answers_2026.xlsx; Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf

I'll take ownership of completing the technical sections of the SIG and assembling the evidence pack (architecture diagram, pen-test summary, subprocessors register, and encrypted key architecture). ETA: initial evidence bundle to Marissa by 2026-03-04 EOD, full technical responses by 2026-03-05.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-minute technical sync if useful.
